background.fact: AMR expands to Adaptive Multi-Rate and was standardized by ETSI for GSM speech.
3GPP adopted AMR for third-generation cellular systems.
Narrowband AMR uses eight speech modes spanning 4.75 to 12.2 kbps.
The narrowband codec samples at 8 kHz and encodes speech in 20-millisecond frames.
AMR-WB is a separate codec with a 16 kHz sampling rate.
RFC 4867, published in April 2007, defines storage files as well as RTP transport.
The registered media type for narrowband AMR is audio/AMR.

windows.note: Requires a compatible FFmpeg library with AMR decoding enabled; the recommended installer omits AMR narrowband.

mac.note: Requires a compatible FFmpeg library with AMR decoding enabled; the recommended installer omits AMR narrowband.

linux.note: Requires a compatible FFmpeg library with AMR decoding enabled; the recommended installer omits AMR narrowband.

problems.fact: A narrowband AMR recording cannot supply the wider frequency range of an AMR-WB source; the codecs use different sampling rates.
Audacity may reject AMR narrowband even after FFmpeg installation because the recommended FFmpeg installer excludes that codec.
AMR and AMR-WB storage signatures differ, so changing an extension cannot change the encoded speech codec.

background.fact: NEF means Nikon Electronic Format and stores raw photographs from Nikon cameras.
A NEF retains captured sensor information together with camera and lens metadata.
Nikon describes NEF storage in uncompressed and losslessly compressed forms.
Depending on the camera, NEF data has 12-bit or 14-bit precision.
White balance, hue, tone, and sharpening choices can be retained as processing instructions.
Nikon processing software can render a NEF as a JPEG or TIFF while retaining the raw original.

windows.note: Manufacturer software for viewing and developing Nikon raw photographs.

mac.note: Manufacturer software for viewing and developing Nikon raw photographs.

linux.note: Viewer with NEF listed in its supported formats; free for private and educational use.

problems.fact: A JPEG export is a rendered result; it does not replace the adjustable sensor data held by the original NEF.
A NEF may look different after development because white balance and other rendering settings are instructions applied by processing software.
The amount of tonal information differs by camera; an eight-bit JPEG export does not retain the original 12-bit or 14-bit raw representation.

background.fact: Sony cameras use the ARW extension for raw photographs.
An ARW retains sensor-derived image information for later processing.
Raw processing parameters can be adjusted after capture.
Sony documents uncompressed, losslessly compressed, and compressed raw recording options.
Lossless compression reduces storage without discarding image information.
Raw file size varies with recording settings and camera sensor size.

windows.note: Manufacturer software for viewing and developing Sony raw photographs.

mac.note: Manufacturer software for viewing and developing Sony raw photographs.

linux.note: Viewer with ARW listed in its supported formats; free for private and educational use.

problems.fact: Raw files can occupy substantial storage; Sony documents different sizes for uncompressed and compressed recording modes.
An ARW is intended for raw development rather than direct distribution as a finished JPEG.
A losslessly compressed raw file is smaller than an uncompressed one but still retains the image information; a smaller size alone does not establish damage.

background.fact: CUR is the Windows cursor container format.
CUR is related to ICO but includes coordinates for the active pointer location.
The active pointer pixel is called the hotspot.
A CUR may embed several images at different dimensions.
Each embedded cursor image has its own hotspot information.
Animated cursor assets use ANI rather than the ordinary CUR workflow.

windows.note: Lists CUR as a readable format; use it to inspect or render cursor images.
Views and edits cursor resources; 32-bit images can be viewed but not edited.

mac.note: Lists CUR as a readable format; use it to inspect or render cursor images.
Viewer with CUR listed in its supported formats; free for private and educational use.

linux.note: Lists CUR as a readable format; use it to inspect or render cursor images.
Viewer with CUR listed in its supported formats; free for private and educational use.

problems.fact: A misplaced hotspot makes clicks land away from the visually expected point; check each frame's coordinates.
A multi-size cursor needs a valid hotspot in every embedded image; copying coordinates blindly between sizes can misalign the pointer.
CUR is specialized for pointer assets; a conventional image format is more suitable when hotspot information is unnecessary.

background.fact: XCF is GIMP's native working-image format.
GIMP uses XCF to retain image editing information between sessions.
XCF retains layers and transparency rather than only a flattened image.
The undo history is excluded from the saved project.
GIMP's Save command writes XCF; other image formats use Export.
GIMP does not position XCF as an interchange format.

windows.note: Native project editor; preserves the working image when saved as XCF.
Reads XCF; do not assume third-party rendering reproduces every GIMP feature.

mac.note: Native project editor; preserves the working image when saved as XCF.
Reads XCF; do not assume third-party rendering reproduces every GIMP feature.

linux.note: Native project editor; preserves the working image when saved as XCF.
Reads XCF; do not assume third-party rendering reproduces every GIMP feature.

problems.fact: Most ordinary image viewers cannot read XCF; export a display copy from GIMP.
Saving a flattened export does not preserve every project property; retain the XCF for future editing.
Closing after an export can still trigger a save warning because exporting does not save changes to the XCF project.

background.fact: DOCX is an Office Open XML word-processing document format.
Microsoft Word has used DOCX by default for new documents since Word 2007.
WordprocessingML describes the main document text and formatting.
A DOCX package uses ZIP-based Open Packaging Conventions.
Images, styles, properties, and relationships can occupy separate package parts.
The format is specified through ECMA-376 and ISO/IEC 29500.

windows.note: Opens and saves Word DOCX; some formatting attributes may differ.
DOCX has been the default for new Word documents since Word 2007.

mac.note: Opens and saves Word DOCX; some formatting attributes may differ.
Opens DOCX; missing fonts and formatting differences may produce warnings.

linux.note: Opens and saves Word DOCX; some formatting attributes may differ.
Free Linux desktop editor that opens and edits DOCX documents.

web.note: Uploads and opens Word documents through the browser.
Opens DOCX documents in the browser; some desktop features differ.

mobile.app: Apple Pages for iPhone and iPad

mobile.note: Opens and edits DOCX documents; Microsoft lists format-specific restrictions for other Word file types.

problems.fact: A DOCX is a package of related parts, so extracting only document.xml does not reproduce the full document.
A DOCX opened in another word processor may lose formatting attributes during import.
Missing fonts can change the appearance when a Word document is opened in Pages.

background.fact: PPM names Netpbm's portable color pixel-map format.
Normal binary PPM identifies an image with P6.
The less common plain-text representation uses P3.
Each pixel carries red, green, and blue samples.
The maximum sample value can range from 1 to 65535.
Raw PPM can contain a sequence of images without separators.
image/x-portable-pixmap is conventional but is not an IANA-registered media type.

windows.note: Reads and writes PPM color images.
Provides the libnetpbm reader and tools for PPM processing.

mac.note: Reads and writes PPM color images.
Provides the libnetpbm reader and tools for PPM processing.

linux.note: Reads and writes PPM color images.
Provides the libnetpbm reader and tools for PPM processing.

problems.fact: PPM uses a redundant representation with little image metadata, so files can be large relative to compressed distribution images.
Some readers implement only one eight-bit image; normalize complex input with pnmtopnm and reduce sample depth with pamdepth when necessary.
Files labeled PPM sometimes use sRGB or linear values instead of the specified transfer function; pnmgamma can reconcile these variants.

background.fact: Radiance RGBE was created by Greg Ward.
RGBE represents a pixel with red, green, and blue bytes plus a shared exponent.
The shared exponent permits a wider brightness range than ordinary 24-bit RGB.
The pixel representation uses four bytes rather than three single-precision floating-point channels.
Radiance lighting simulations use RGBE images to represent calculated brightness.
The registered media type is image/vnd.radiance.

windows.note: Reads and writes Radiance HDR through its HDR coder.
Named as a user of the Radiance media type by the registered format description.

mac.note: Reads and writes Radiance HDR through its HDR coder.
Named as a user of the Radiance media type by the registered format description.

linux.note: Reads and writes Radiance HDR through its HDR coder.
The original rendering system includes RGBE reading and writing code.

problems.fact: Clipping bright values to the ordinary eight-bit range can discard highlight information; choose an appropriate rendering rather than simply truncating samples.
An HDR image needs software that interprets the shared exponent; its bytes are not ordinary packed RGB pixels.
The extension alone does not identify the contents; the registered Radiance description advises checking the complete header.

background.fact: HEIF means High Efficiency Image File Format and is specified by ISO/IEC 23008-12.
HEIF organizes images in an ISO Base Media File Format container.
A HEIF container can hold individual still images, collections, and timed sequences.
The container can associate metadata and derived images with stored pictures.
HEVC is one supported coding format; the container is not itself the H.265 codec.
Generic HEIF still images use image/heif, while sequences use image/heif-sequence.

windows.note: HEIF import and export were added in GIMP 2.10.2.
Viewer with HEIF listed in its supported formats; free for private and educational use.

mac.note: HEIF import and export were added in GIMP 2.10.2.
Apple documents HEIF-to-JPEG export in Preview; macOS High Sierra introduced HEIF support.

linux.note: HEIF import and export were added in GIMP 2.10.2.
Viewer with HEIF listed in its supported formats; free for private and educational use.

mobile.note: iOS 11 introduced support for HEIF photos from supported devices.

Photo app for iOS and Android with documented HEIF/.heic image support. This does not establish decoding of every HEIF codec or sequence; HEVC video remains unsupported on Android. Check current app requirements before installation.

problems.fact: A program needs support for both the container and the stored codec; the HEIF brand identifies decoding requirements.
A file can include several related pictures or a sequence, so a single-image export need not represent the entire container.
Older Apple systems lack the built-in support introduced with iOS 11 and macOS High Sierra; conversion to JPEG improves compatibility.
